subject: Post-demo: Private/VPC air-gap feasibility + next technical tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ben Jacobs <ben.jacobs@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap + proposed next tests (Private/VPC & air-gap)

Ben — thanks again for carving out time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side after the demo: 

Recap (what we covered)
- Redwood Private (VPC) overview: private control plane + customer-managed networking; optional on-prem bundle for air-gapped installs.
- Differentiators vs hyperscalers: unified runtime with model/version pinning, explicit KV/prefix caching for lower per-token cost, and runtime fallbacks for capacity.
- Networking options: VPC peering, PrivateLink-style endpoints, and full air-gapped on-prem appliance.

Key technical questions you raised
- Can we run entirely air-gapped (no egress) with local model store + control plane on customer network?
- How do we authenticate and rotate keys (KMS/HSM) in Private?
- What are expected p95 latencies for 512-token, 8k-context workloads on our Dedicated hardware vs on-prem?

Proposed immediate tests (what would prove fit)
1) Latency/throughput run: 512-token generation, 8k context, 100 concurrent clients — measure p50/p95/p99 + tokens/sec. (Run against Redwood Private in your VPC and against an equivalent hyperscaler-managed endpoint for baseline.)
2) Networking proof: simple VPC peering + PrivateLink test to validate routing & MTU; verify no unexpected outbound flows.
3) Air-gap feasibility checklist: confirm required OS/kernel versions, container runtime (we support containerd/Docker), and a short list of allowed external artifacts for offline install.
4) Security handoff: we’ll send SOC2 evidence and a short KMS/HSM integration guide for your infra team.

Suggested owners & timeline
- Redwood: Rishi (test plan + SRE coordination), Vivek (commercial/commitment options), Marissa (PM/coordination) — deliverables in 3 business days for test plan, schedule for week of 2/22.
- Acme: Ben to confirm infra contacts, Legal to confirm NDAs and onboarding timing.

Attachments: redwood-private-networking-diagram.pdf (networking options), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (timeline & owners).

Ask: Can you confirm the infra contact for the network test and whether Acme prefers an on-prem trial or VPC-hosted Private environment as the first step?

Thanks — I’ll coordinate a short 30-min kickoff once we have infra names.

—
Marissa Cole | Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-private-networking-diagram.pdf] [Attachment: mutual-action-plan.xlsx]

From: Ben Jacobs <ben.jacobs@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal <legal@acmecorp.com>, Chris Nguyen <chris@edgecloud.io>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed next tests (Private/VPC & air-gap)

Marissa — appreciate the clear summary. A couple of quick items from my side: 

1) Air-gap: Our security team prefers an on-prem install for the initial POC to validate zero-Internet installs. They will want the installer artifacts scanned before they are allowed onto our network. Is a fully offline install possible (no control plane egress) for the 1-month eval?

2) KMS/HSM: We use AWS KMS for key management today and have an HSM appliance in our colo for production secrets. We need to know whether Redwood can integrate with our HSM (PKCS#11) or if keys must be managed by Redwood for Private.

3) Cost/License: Can you provide a rough license range for a 4-GPU on-prem bundle vs Redwood Dedicated in our region? We need a ballpark to budget the POC.

I’ve looped Legal for NDA/contract concerns and Chris from our infra team to coordinate the networking test. I’ll confirm the infra contacts by EOD.

—Ben
Director, ML Platforms
Acme Cybernetics

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Post-demo recap + proposed next tests (Private/VPC & air-gap)

Marissa/Vivek — notes from the SRE/arch perspective on the tests Ben asked for:

- Air-gapped install: Yes — we support fully offline installs. We provide a signed bundle (tar) that includes the runtime, model artifacts (optionally), and an installer script. Customer-run checksum verification and offline KMS provisioning are supported. The only caveat: automatic model downloads require an initial transfer; we can provide a recommended transfer checklist.

- HSM integration: We have a PKCS#11 shim in our Private runtime that can talk to customer HSMs; full rotation workflow is supported but needs an initial integration step. For the POC, we can run with customer-managed keys and provide an isolated keystore for the duration.

- Test plan (high-level):
  * Test A: 512-token generation, 8k context, 100 concurrent clients, 1M tokens total — capture p50/p95/p99 + tokens/sec.
  * Test B: Network egress audit during VPC peering & PrivateLink to verify all flows are to specified CIDRs; include MTU and path MTU checks.
  * Test C: Offline install dry-run — validate installer on dev host and perform checksum + dependency inventory.

I’ve drafted a short SRE test plan (sre-test-plan.md) and attached it here. Would recommend we schedule a 60-min technical kickoff with Acme infra to walk the SRE plan and confirm test harness access (metrics endpoint, SSH jumpbox if needed).

I’ll prepare a quick cost delta for on-prem 4xA100-equivalent vs Redwood Dedicated caps — Vivek, can you handle the commercial numbers and put a draft in the MAP?

—Rishi
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood
[Attachment: sre-test-plan.md]

Ben — excellent questions, and thanks for looping Legal. Quick replies inline: 

- Air-gap: we can do fully offline installs for the POC. Rishi’s attached plan covers the checksum/installer flow; we’ll provide the signed bundle and a short checklist your security team can run before allowing artifacts on the network.

- HSM: we support PKCS#11 integration; we’ll need an integration window for the initial rotation test. If Acme prefers, we can do a temporary customer-managed key for the POC.

- Cost: Vivek will follow up with an initial ballpark on 4x-GPU on-prem vs Dedicated pricing. For the POC we can offer a limited-time evaluation licensing model so you can measure perf before committing.

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben to confirm infra contact for scheduling (today or tomorrow).
2) Redwood to send NDA + SRE test plan (we sent sre-test-plan.md — attached).
3) Schedule 60-min technical kickoff for week of 2/22; aim to run Test A/B during that week.

If that works, I’ll get Neha to start a standard POC MSA draft and route to your Legal for redlines.

Thanks — will stand up the kickoff as soon as we have infra names.

—
Marissa
